newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH PM LIPPONEN SEES SUSTAINED GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH PM LIPPONEN SEES SUSTAINED GROWTH.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Wednesday Finnish economic growth would be sustained as far as forecasts reached.

Following are highlights from the text of his speech prepared for delivery at at a Social Democratic Party meeting: * "Finland has finally ... succeeded to combine strong growth and overall stability." * "As far as forecasts reach, sustained economic growth is in sight." * "In the fight against unemployment we have won the first and decisive round as the big economic indicators point in the right direction ... The downward direction of the unemployment curve is too gentle." * "Economic growth must be secured through moderate incomes settlements. The labour market organisations have committed themselves to a low-inflation policy." * "Branch union leaders have not questioned this target," Lipponen told the SDP council meeting in a deviation from the prepared text of the speech. * "When (the labour market organisations) have made progress in their (pay deal) talks the government can promote an agreement through tax relief." * "The supply of energy must be secured on the basis of the principles of sustained development. Now it is important to investigate various options without excluding any." * "There is no reason to take the risk of splitting the government," he said in another deviation from the prepared speech. * "All coalition parties, including, I hope, the social democrats at this meeting, have come to the conclusion that we want to continue to cooperate in government." * "It is social democratic policy to put the brakes on state indebtedness by cutting expenditure in a phase of economic growth." * "It is social democratic policy to to ease taxation of wage earners and pensioners." * "The government will give an EMU-report (to parliament) in May. * "We should reach a final decision on EMU in parliament which as broad a majority as possible could embrace. The (opposition) Centre Party's effort to avoid fuelling EMU conflicts deserves credit." * "The government is ready to talk about so called buffer funds with the labour market organisations once the organisations first, among themselves, develop more concrete thoughts." --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
